parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes tier-1 universal exposures: federal binary passport/entry screening with refusal and possible fraud-based permanent ineligibility, federal and division facility exclusion by birth sex, and documented births-based custody harm. Division law has no state nondiscrimination or state hate-crime protection and also restricts minors' sports and care and school facilities. Mitigations are real but partial: existing X passports remain valid, fraud finding is not automatic, trespass requires refusal to depart, several federal orders are enjoined/litigated, and national employment/hate-crime recourse exists. No credible execution or long imprisonment for mere presence places this above 0.25 anchors, but state-imposed exposure and custody abuse keep it well below 0.55.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition; X/new mismatched passports not processed, existing X valid to expiry. Cable requires refusal on document discrepancy/reasonable doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports accepted to expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waivers, never automatic; civil-liberties suit pending and some orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger refusal, delay, or fraud inquiry, converting an identity mismatch into immigration consequence; allied advisories reflect reported confiscations/blocking.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Reported trespass arrest under a criminal bathroom law, handcuffed and held 24 hours in men's ward; national immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; corrections policies reportedly remove hormones and cut hair.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National courts have enjoined/blocked several orders; trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not entry alone; reported custody harms are not shown frequency-quantified for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility or document encounter can become arrest/detention and birth-sex placement; efficient enforcement of hostile rules is exposure, not mitigation, while court injunctions provide partial restraint.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal ban on government facilities congruent with gender identity. Division 2025 law reserves public multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by biological sex and prohibits non-matching entry, with civil cause of action.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division accommodations only where no opposite-sex multi-occupancy access; three cities have local gender-identity ordinances; 29 states plus capital have no mapped ban, but that does not apply here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal exposure every public facility visit; local ordinances do not cancel state or federal rules, and a civil encounter can escalate to trespass/arrest where criminal provisions apply.

care_services.exposure: Division bans sex-reassignment surgery and gender-affirming care for children effective 2024; federal orders target minor care and proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement under 18.
care_services.protection: Adult routine/emergency care restrictions not documented as a visitor ban; several federal health orders are blocked/enjoined or proposed and unresolved.
care_services.interaction: For travelling minors, care denial or provider caution can interact with school/sports and document rules; adult visitors face less documented care-specific exposure from this dossier.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing treats gender identity as binary and, in counterterrorism material, 'radically pro-transgender' actors as priorities; division ranked among worst for anti-trans adult legislation, Negative policy band, no state nondiscrimination or hate-crime law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity and 2020 ruling prohibits employment discrimination; three cities have local protections; courts remain a partial check.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile state framing plus no local recourse amplifies street and institutional exposure, though functioning courts and national statutes prevent treating paper protections as wholly inoperative.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division school law requires restrooms by sex assigned at birth from pre-K, with only narrow reasonable accommodation; sports ban; minor care ban. Federal order directs investigation/prosecution related to school social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: School reasonable accommodation for students not wishing to use birth-sex multi-occupancy facilities; federal prosecution order is among measures challenged/bloced in part, status uncertain for enforcement.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces school-facility, sports and care exposure and a parent/guardian may face inquiry or care denial even if the parent is not the facility-ban defendant.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific trans violence rate, incident count, or police-response outcome documented; do not infer safety from absence. National public opinion supports birth-sex document laws (66%) and sports alignment (69%).
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no documented pattern in this division of police sweeps, extortion, or trans-specific killings in the dossier.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of local violence evidence is not_documented, not protective; legal exposure in facilities, entry and custody is the documented street-level risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state nondiscrimination or state hate-crime remedy in division; local ordinances cover only three cities; facility law challenge/enforcement suits not documented; birth-certificate change requires surgery plus court order for residents.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment recourse since 2020, national hate-crime coverage, litigation/enjoinment of several federal orders, and stated four-element fraud test provide partial remedies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are fragmented across federal/national and three cities and do not restore facility access or prevent entry refusal in real time; uncertainty about what is in effect at travel is itself exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar birth-sex custody/facility placement and weak local recourse, but this case lacks documented frequent prison assaults, weekly raids, or extortion pattern and has functioning courts enjoining federal measures, so it sits above 0.25.

Similar routine document/facility mismatch exposure without typical imprisonment, but here exposure compounds across federal entry, facility bans, criminal trespass example, minors' restrictions, and reported custody abuse, placing it below 0.45.

Far below 0.85: unlike explicit visitor protections, chosen-name documents, and effective complaints/discipline, this regime prohibits congruent facilities by birth sex, restricts mismatched passports, and offers no division-level nondiscrimination remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document or presentation mismatch at entry, in public facilities, or in custody, leading to refusal, civil liability, possible trespass arrest, or birth-sex placement, with minors additionally facing school, sports, and care restrictions. Courts, existing X-passport validity, the non-automatic fraud test, and national employment/hate-crime law mitigate but do not cancel the universal, state-imposed exposures. That combination is more severe than bureaucratic delay or partial denial, yet less custodially lethal or systematically extortionate than 0.25 anchors, supporting a score in the mid-0.30s.
